headline: Volvo says its driverless trucks, built with Aurora, will run on Texas roads with no safety driver from early 2027.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: these are future company targets, tied to a 23 Sep preview, with no new deployment today.
importance_line: Truck drivers and freight shippers in Texas and Arizona may see driverless trucks from 2027, but the dates are company targets, not confirmed launches.
summary: Autoweek reports that Volvo's autonomous unit expects to run driverless trucks without safety drivers on Texas roads in the first quarter of 2027, using the Aurora Driver system from its partner Aurora, and to have 300 trucks hauling freight between hubs by the end of 2027. Volvo's Nils Jaeger gave those targets to the magazine, and Volvo also says its autonomous business could reach 3 billion dollars within five years, a company forecast.
notes: Preview event was 23 Sep 2026; interview dates not given.
